summary_notes: Adtech company building session-aware personalization and realtime ranking for ad auctions. Extremely sensitive to tail latency and per-request cost — target 20-50ms p95 for 32 token completions on production path, and <10ms incremental for embedding lookups used in candidate re-rank. Interested in Redwood Optimize features: batching suggestions, KV/prefix caching, quantization profiles. Wants reproducible perf numbers to compare Dedicated capacity vs Hosted + autoscaling. Team cares about predictable unit economics more than absolute lowest latency for every request. Quoted: 'We need predictable 99th percentile under load spikes — losing bids when we miss windows.'
technical_requirements: Latency SLOs: p95 20-50ms for short-chat (<=64 tokens) on critical path
Throughput: sustained 800-1200 RPS during peak auctions, spikes to 4k RPS for 30s bursts
Cost target: <$0.0008 per inference on typical short paths; embedding cost budget per 10k queries: <$8
Model preferences: open Llama2-style variants or curated quantized models; willing to accept 4-bit quantization if quality delta <2%
Fallback strategy: fallback to cheaper model variant when Dedicated saturated; require automatic routing and circuit-breaker
Cache behavior: per-session prefix caching + KV cache with 24h TTL for embeddings
Data residency: US-only; audit logs retained 180 days
perf_benchmark_requests: Test A: 1k sustained RPS, seq len 32, measure p50/p95/p99 (hosted vs dedicated)
Test B: Burst test 4k RPS for 30s, observe cold-start and tail latency behavior
Test C: Batching sweep — variable batch sizes (1,4,8,16) and request coalescing to find cost/latency sweet spot
Test D: Quantization quality/perf sweep — float16 baseline vs 8-bit, 4-bit q8_0 and q4_0; measure top-K rerank quality delta
Test E: KV cache effectiveness — simulate 10k sessions with repeated prefixes; measure token savings and latency delta
